- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances keep their sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 11 June 2025 and 8 July 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. ATLAS. General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances keep their sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 11 June 2025 and 8 July 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. LEDGR is not a read-only mirror: it sets Geändert when the data actually changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). For example, an ATLAS birth date written 06/02/1966 is 6 February 1966. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the month-first habit of its American suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the British order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master. Rows marked Status "inaktiv" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. Do not trust the Geändert dates of LEDGR: the system was restored from an old backup between 21 February 2025 and 13 March 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 08/02/1998" belongs to someone born in August. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances keep their sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 11 June 2025 and 8 July 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

SOURCE NOTES:

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=12/09/1961 was born in December. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "Altdaten" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 10 April 2025–1 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

- implicit_country: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code if the notes say this system's rows are all in one country without stating it; otherwise null.
- international_prefixes: which of "+", "00", "011" the notes list as international access markers for this system's phone numbers (empty array if none stated).

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=12/09/1961 was born in December. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "Altdaten" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 10 April 2025–1 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). - given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=07/08/1986 is 8 July 1986. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. This BRIGHTDESK extract comes from a read-only mirror that was rebuilt between 23 February 2025 and 15 March 2025: the updated value of every BRIGHTDESK row is the time the mirror copied it, not the time the record last changed.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is a receivable (the account holder owes us); a negative one is a credit.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of ours to the supplier; the master stores it as a negative balance. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: GUEST" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. "env":"replay" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows. VERITAS is not a read-only mirror: it sets ts when the data actually changes.

Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=07/08/1986 is 8 July 1986. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. This BRIGHTDESK extract comes from a read-only mirror that was rebuilt between 23 February 2025 and 15 March 2025: the updated value of every BRIGHTDESK row is the time the mirror copied it, not the time the record last changed.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is a receivable (the account holder owes us); a negative one is a credit.

ATLAS. Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=12/09/1961 was born in December. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "Altdaten" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 10 April 2025–1 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team works from Boston and writes numeric dates the way people there do. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money we owe the member, so it is negative in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A row marked "env":"replay" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it. VERITAS's ts is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2022 audit.

Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".

Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=12/09/1961 was born in December. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. A row marked Status "Altdaten" does not carry a void marker; keep it. The Geändert column of LEDGR shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 10 April 2025–1 May 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team works from Boston and writes numeric dates the way people there do. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money we owe the member, so it is negative in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A row marked "env":"replay" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it. VERITAS's ts is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2022 audit.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=legacy counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=legacy counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the same way as the master: positive means the account holder owes us. Do not confuse Status "Altdaten" with "storniert" entries: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. LEDGR's Geändert is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2023 audit.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Read numeric ATLAS birth dates as MM/DD/YYYY, never as DD/MM/YYYY. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Prague to Indianapolis in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. VERITAS was migrated to new hardware between 23 March 2025 and 30 April 2025, and the migration overwrote ts on every row with the migration date.

- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was migrated to new hardware between 25 August 2024 and 8 October 2024, and the migration overwrote updated on every row with the migration date.

LEDGR. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was migrated to new hardware between 25 August 2024 and 8 October 2024, and the migration overwrote updated on every row with the migration date.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. - update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.

If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=02/10/1989 was born in February. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance runs in US locale, so numeric birth dates are month/day/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the same way as the master: positive means the account holder owes us. LEDGR is not a read-only mirror: it sets Geändert when the data actually changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). For example, an ATLAS birth date written 12/11/1952 is 12 November 1952. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. In a numeric date the first number is the month (so 04/03/2021 falls in April). A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: PAUSED" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"import" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. Do not trust the ts dates of VERITAS: the system was restored from an old backup between 3 March 2025 and 31 March 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.
