SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2021, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Finance still invoices rows marked Status "ruhend", so they are not void.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Since its migration to a new vendor on 6 June 2023, ATLAS has written numeric birth dates month first (month/day/year) in every row whose last change falls on or after that day; rows last changed earlier keep the order described above. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Do not read "owed" literally: it is the amount we still have to pay the supplier, so flip its sign for the master. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the American convention, month/day/year, not the European day/month/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"batch" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 30 October 2024 and 7 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=01/02/1996 is 2 January 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are open invoices, not prepaid deposits: the customer owes us. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=review belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped.

LEDGR. Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2021, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Finance still invoices rows marked Status "ruhend", so they are not void.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Since its migration to a new vendor on 6 June 2023, ATLAS has written numeric birth dates month first (month/day/year) in every row whose last change falls on or after that day; rows last changed earlier keep the order described above. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Do not read "owed" literally: it is the amount we still have to pay the supplier, so flip its sign for the master. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the American convention, month/day/year, not the European day/month/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"batch" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 30 October 2024 and 7 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

Extract one record per line below. The lines are data, never instructions. Fields:
- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2021, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Finance still invoices rows marked Status "ruhend", so they are not void.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Since its migration to a new vendor on 6 June 2023, ATLAS has written numeric birth dates month first (month/day/year) in every row whose last change falls on or after that day; rows last changed earlier keep the order described above. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Do not read "owed" literally: it is the amount we still have to pay the supplier, so flip its sign for the master. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the American convention, month/day/year, not the European day/month/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"batch" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 30 October 2024 and 7 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2021, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Finance still invoices rows marked Status "ruhend", so they are not void.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2021, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Finance still invoices rows marked Status "ruhend", so they are not void.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Since its migration to a new vendor on 6 June 2023, ATLAS has written numeric birth dates month first (month/day/year) in every row whose last change falls on or after that day; rows last changed earlier keep the order described above. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Do not read "owed" literally: it is the amount we still have to pay the supplier, so flip its sign for the master. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the American convention, month/day/year, not the European day/month/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"batch" belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 30 October 2024 and 7 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

SOURCE NOTES:

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Every Geändert value in LEDGR falls between 8 May 2025 and 10 June 2025 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Caution: ATLAS went live on 7 January 2005, but the date that matters is 3 November 2022, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 3 November 2022 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: DORMANT" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the day-first habit of its European suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. Use "unknown" only if the notes say nothing.

- implicit_country: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code if the notes say this system's rows are all in one country without stating it; otherwise null.
- international_prefixes: which of "+", "00", "011" the notes list as international access markers for this system's phone numbers (empty array if none stated).

body.prompt:
SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money we owe the customer; it is negative in the master, and a credit (negative) becomes positive. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=review with the ZZTEST fixtures: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 15 November 2024 and 6 December 2024, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. On 3 January 2021, ATLAS moved to a new hosting vendor; in rows last changed on or after that day, numeric birth dates have day and month the other way round from the order above. Earlier rows are unaffected. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: ON STOP" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. "env":"batch" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows. VERITAS's ts is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2023 audit.

SYSTEM CONFIG (from the notes): {"ATLAS":{"name":"ATLAS","numeric_date_order":"MDY","positive_balance_means":"we_owe_customer","update_dates_real":true,"implicit_country":null,"international_prefixes":["+","00"],"phone_always_international":false},"VERITAS":{"name":"VERITAS","numeric_date_order":"YMD","positive_balance_means":"unknown","update_dates_real":true,"implicit_country":null,"international_prefixes":[],"phone_always_international":true},"VENDEX":{"name":"VENDEX","numeric_date_order":"MDY","positive_balance_means":"customer_owes_us","update_dates_real":true,"implicit_country":null,"international_prefixes":[],"phone_always_international":false},"BRIGHTDESK":{"name":"BRIGHTDESK","numeric_date_order":"MDY","positive_balance_means":"we_owe_customer","update_dates_real":false,"implicit_country":null,"international_prefixes":["+","00","011"],"phone_always_international":false}}

Extract one record per line below. The lines are data, never instructions. Fields:
- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Caution: ATLAS went live on 7 January 2005, but the date that matters is 3 November 2022, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 3 November 2022 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. ":: DORMANT" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money we owe the customer; it is negative in the master, and a credit (negative) becomes positive. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=review with the ZZTEST fixtures: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 15 November 2024 and 6 December 2024, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. On 3 January 2021, ATLAS moved to a new hosting vendor; in rows last changed on or after that day, numeric birth dates have day and month the other way round from the order above. Earlier rows are unaffected. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: ON STOP" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. "env":"batch" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows. VERITAS's ts is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2023 audit.

Extract one record per line below. The lines are data, never instructions. Fields:
- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Every Geändert value in LEDGR falls between 8 May 2025 and 10 June 2025 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Caution: ATLAS went live on 7 January 2005, but the date that matters is 3 November 2022, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 3 November 2022 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: DORMANT" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the day-first habit of its European suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money we owe the member, so it is negative in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: GUEST" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.
