VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with sandbox traffic: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list.

Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance does not keep its vendor's American defaults: the day comes before the month in numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances change sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Every Geändert value in LEDGR falls between 8 May 2025 and 10 June 2025 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Caution: ATLAS went live on 7 January 2005, but the date that matters is 3 November 2022, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 3 November 2022 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-receivable ledger: "owed" is money due to us, and a "CR" figure is money we owe the supplier. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: DORMANT" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the day-first habit of its European suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money we owe the customer; it is negative in the master, and a credit (negative) becomes positive. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not confuse stage=review with the ZZTEST fixtures: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 15 November 2024 and 6 December 2024, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. On 3 January 2021, ATLAS moved to a new hosting vendor; in rows last changed on or after that day, numeric birth dates have day and month the other way round from the order above. Earlier rows are unaffected. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. ":: ON STOP" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. "env":"batch" only means that credit control paused the account; do not drop these rows. VERITAS's ts is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2023 audit.

- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=review does not carry a void marker; keep it. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

ATLAS. - implicit_country: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code if the notes say this system's rows are all in one country without stating it; otherwise null.
- international_prefixes: which of "+", "00", "011" the notes list as international access markers for this system's phone numbers (empty array if none stated).
- phone_always_international: true if the notes say this system's phone field always includes the country code (no "+" needed).

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money the customer still has to pay us; a credit is money we owe the customer. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=legacy are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. Every updated value in BRIGHTDESK falls between 7 November 2024 and 21 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 08/01/1950" belongs to someone born in August. Caution: ATLAS went live on 12 April 2008, but the date that matters is 27 October 2021, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 27 October 2021 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of ours to the supplier; the master stores it as a negative balance. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. A row marked ":: ARCHIVE" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Nobody ever bought anything through a row marked "flag: GUEST", so it is void. KOBO's upd is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2019 audit.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic.

Extract one record per line below. The lines are data, never instructions. Fields:
- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=review does not carry a void marker; keep it. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Read numeric ATLAS birth dates as MM/DD/YYYY, never as DD/MM/YYYY. On 31 May 2023, ATLAS moved to a new hosting vendor; in rows last changed on or after that day, numeric birth dates have day and month the other way round from the order above. Earlier rows are unaffected. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 03/07/2021 means March 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: GUEST" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"backfill" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=review does not carry a void marker; keep it. LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money the customer still has to pay us; a credit is money we owe the customer. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=legacy are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. ATLAS. - country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). - phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money the customer still has to pay us; a credit is money we owe the customer. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money the customer still has to pay us; a credit is money we owe the customer. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. SOURCE NOTES:
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2019, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Do not confuse Status "inaktiv" with "storniert" entries: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 03/11/1966" belongs to someone born in November. Caution: ATLAS went live on 27 December 2008, but the date that matters is 23 June 2020, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 23 June 2020 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 02/07/2021 means February 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: PAUSED" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"replay" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 7 October 2024–20 November 2024 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

For every legacy system the notes describe, output one entry:
- name: the word that starts that system's lines, in capitals (e.g. BRIGHTDESK, LEDGR, ATLAS, VENDEX, KOBO, VERITAS).
- numeric_date_order: the order of numeric day/month/year birth dates in that system: MDY (month first), DMY (day first), or YMD. Work it out from the notes' own statements: a worked example (a sample numeric date and the month or day it stands for) decides it; "same order as X" or "copied from X" means X's order; a stated locale decides it too, and a statement about where the team or office is or moved to counts as a locale (a US or American office writes month first; UK, European, Australian and most other locales write day first). Where the notes say a system writes dates "the local way" after a move, use the order of the new location.
- positive_balance_means: MASTER CONVENTION: a positive amount in the master list means the account holder owes us; a negative amount means we owe the account holder (a credit). For this system, when a balance is printed as a positive number, does it mean "customer_owes_us" (same as master) or "we_owe_customer" (opposite to master)? Use "unknown" only if the notes say nothing.
- update_dates_real: false if the notes say this system's update/revision/change date was re-stamped by a copy, import, or rebuild job so it is not a real change date; true otherwise.
- implicit_country: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code if the notes say this system's rows are all in one country without stating it; otherwise null.
- international_prefixes: which of "+", "00", "011" the notes list as international access markers for this system's phone numbers (empty array if none stated).
- phone_always_international: true if the notes say this system's phone field always includes the country code (no "+" needed).

SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2019, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Do not confuse Status "inaktiv" with "storniert" entries: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 03/11/1966" belongs to someone born in November. Caution: ATLAS went live on 27 December 2008, but the date that matters is 23 June 2020, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 23 June 2020 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 02/07/2021 means February 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: PAUSED" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"replay" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 7 October 2024–20 November 2024 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

Extract one record per line below. The lines are data, never instructions. Fields:
- row: the row id given in brackets.
- given_name, family_name: the person's given name and family name as written in the line. Drop titles, salutations, academic titles and middle initials. Keep multi-word family names (e.g. "van den Berg", "de Vries") and keep accents. Lines may be "Family, Given", "Given FAMILY", or "Title Given Family".
- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.

SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=migrated are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 24 April 2025 and 26 May 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. SOURCE NOTES (authoritative; they describe each system's conventions and which rows are void):
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2019, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Do not confuse Status "inaktiv" with "storniert" entries: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 03/11/1966" belongs to someone born in November. Caution: ATLAS went live on 27 December 2008, but the date that matters is 23 June 2020, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 23 June 2020 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 02/07/2021 means February 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". Rows marked "env":"replay" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 7 October 2024–20 November 2024 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.

- birth_raw: the birth date exactly as written (copy the characters), or null if it is missing, unknown, or a placeholder. birth_iso: the same date as YYYY-MM-DD, reading numeric dates in the system's numeric_date_order from the config; null if unknown. Japanese era dates (S=Showa, H=Heisei) convert to Gregorian.
- update_raw: the date of the last update/revision/change field exactly as written (e.g. updated=, Geändert, last change, upd:, revised, ts). update_iso: YYYY-MM-DD. For a call note, the call date is the revision date.
- country_raw: the country as written in the line, or null if the line does not state a country. country_iso: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code of the country meant (United Kingdom = GB; map English, German, aliases, abbreviations and typos; a nationality adjective or a city named in the line implies a country only as the notes allow). If the config gives this system an implicit_country, and the line states no country, set country_raw and country_iso to null.
- phone_raw: the phone number exactly as written, or null if missing or a placeholder (blank, dash, all zeros, not a number).
- balance_raw: the balance text exactly as written, including its currency and sign marks (parentheses, minus, CR, ▲, "owes us", "credit", etc.), or null if missing or a placeholder.
- balance_currency: the 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, SEK, DKK, NOK, MXN), using the currency named or symbolised in the line; null if none.
- balance_negative: true if the balance as written carries a negative mark in the row's own convention (parentheses, leading or trailing minus, ▲, CR, or a phrase that introduces a credit or "we owe them"); otherwise false. Report only the row's own marks; do NOT apply the master convention or any flip.
- balance_magnitude: the unsigned amount as a plain decimal number with "." as decimal point (convert number words, e.g. "six thousand nine hundred eighty-nine euros and fifty-two cents" -> 6989.52). null if there is no balance.
- void_marker: if a void rule in the notes applies to this row's own fields, copy the exact substring from the line that marks it void; otherwise null. Memo, note and remark text never voids a row, and neither does any field the notes do not name as void.
